complaint: Check engine light flashing, engine shakes at idle and under light acceleration.
observations: Misfire counter on cylinder 1 climbing at idle
Fuel trims normal (STFT +2%, LTFT +3%)
No vacuum leaks found
diagnostic_steps: Confirm the code and record freeze frame data.
Check live misfire counters to confirm the misfire is isolated to cylinder 1.
Swap the cylinder 1 ignition coil with cylinder 2 and clear codes.
Run the engine: the misfire moves to cylinder 2 (P0302), so the fault follows the coil.
Inspect the spark plug in cylinder 1 for wear or oil fouling before closing the job.
fix: Replace the cylinder 1 ignition coil; replace spark plugs if they are at or past the service interval.

common_wrong_answers.why_wrong: Fuel trims are normal and the misfire moved with the coil, so the injector is not the cause.
The cat is a victim of a misfire, not the cause; driving with a flashing MIL can damage it.

safety_notes: A flashing check engine light means an active misfire that can overheat the catalytic converter; advise the customer not to drive hard.

complaint: Check engine light on, no drivability issues.
observations: Downstream O2 sensor reading lean and switching more than expected
Ticking sound from under the car at cold start that fades when warm
Fuel trims within +/-5%
diagnostic_steps: Confirm there are no misfire or fuel trim codes that would damage the cat or skew the readings.
Compare upstream and downstream O2 sensor activity in live data.
Inspect the exhaust for leaks between the engine and the downstream O2 sensor, cold engine, with a smoke machine or by feel/sound.
Find a cracked flex pipe ahead of the downstream O2 sensor; outside air is being pulled in on exhaust pulses.
Repair the leak, clear codes, and complete a drive cycle to confirm the catalyst monitor passes.
root_cause: Exhaust leak (cracked flex pipe) upstream of the downstream O2 sensor making the cat appear inefficient.
fix: Replace or weld the flex pipe section, then re-run the catalyst monitor.

common_wrong_answers.why_wrong: An exhaust leak ahead of the rear sensor can mimic a failed cat; leaks must be ruled out first.
The sensor is reading correctly; it is measuring the outside air being drawn in.

safety_notes: Exhaust leaks can let carbon monoxide into the cabin; inspect with the engine cool to avoid burns.

complaint: Rough idle, check engine light on.
observations: LTFT +18% both banks at idle, drops to +4% at 2500 RPM
Faint hissing near the back of the intake manifold
MAF reading normal for engine size at idle
diagnostic_steps: Note that both banks are lean, which points to a shared cause (intake air, fuel pressure or MAF) rather than one bank.
Compare fuel trims at idle vs 2500 RPM: lean at idle that improves with RPM points to a vacuum leak (unmetered air matters most when airflow is low).
Run a smoke test on the intake.
Smoke comes out of a cracked PCV hose at the rear of the intake.
Replace the hose, clear trims, and verify LTFT returns to within +/-5%.
root_cause: Vacuum leak from a cracked PCV hose letting in unmetered air.
fix: Replace the PCV hose and reset fuel trims.

common_wrong_answers.why_wrong: The O2 sensors are correctly reporting a lean condition; they are not causing it.
A bad MAF usually causes lean trims across the RPM range, not mainly at idle; MAF readings were normal.

complaint: Heater blows lukewarm air in winter, temperature gauge reads low on the highway.
observations: Coolant temp on scan tool takes over 20 minutes to reach 70 C (158 F) and drops on the highway
Upper radiator hose gets warm within a few minutes of a cold start
Coolant level full
diagnostic_steps: Verify the coolant level is correct.
Compare ECT sensor reading with an infrared thermometer at the thermostat housing to confirm the sensor is accurate.
Feel the upper radiator hose on a cold start: it should stay cool until the thermostat opens. Warming early means coolant is flowing to the radiator too soon.
Conclude the thermostat is stuck open.
root_cause: Thermostat stuck open, so the engine never reaches regulating temperature.
fix: Replace the thermostat (housing assembly on this engine), refill and bleed the cooling system.

common_wrong_answers.why_wrong: The IR thermometer confirmed the sensor was accurate; the engine really is running cold.
A clogged heater core does not cause a low engine temperature or P0128.

safety_notes: Never open a hot cooling system; let it cool before removing the cap.

complaint: Brake pedal pulsates and steering wheel shakes when braking from highway speed.
observations: Front rotors show uneven dark patches
Wheels were recently installed at a tire shop with an impact gun
Rotor thickness variation measured at 0.04 mm (0.0016 in)
diagnostic_steps: Road test to confirm pulsation is from the front (steering wheel shake) rather than the rear.
Measure lateral runout with a dial indicator with the lug nuts torqued to spec.
Measure rotor thickness at 8 points with a micrometer to find thickness variation.
Thickness variation above the typical limit (around 0.013-0.025 mm / 0.0005-0.001 in) causes pedal pulsation. Uneven lug torque and pad material transfer are the common causes.
Replace or machine rotors if above minimum thickness, install new pads, torque lugs with a torque wrench in a star pattern, and bed in the pads.
root_cause: Rotor thickness variation from uneven pad deposits and runout caused by uneven lug nut torque.
fix: Replace or resurface front rotors, replace pads, torque wheels to spec in a star pattern, bed in new pads.

common_wrong_answers.why_wrong: New pads on rotors with thickness variation will still pulsate.

common_wrong_answers.answer: The rotors are warped from heat.
common_wrong_answers.why_wrong: True heat warping is rare; most 'warped rotors' are thickness variation from deposits and runout. Calling it warping skips the root cause (lug torque).

safety_notes: Always torque lug nuts with a torque wrench to the manufacturer's spec.

complaint: Car pulls to the right when braking. Burning smell after driving.
observations: Right front wheel much hotter than left after a test drive
Right front inner pad worn to 2 mm, outer pad 7 mm
Car tracks straight when not braking
diagnostic_steps: Confirm the pull only happens under braking (rules out alignment and tire issues).
Compare wheel temperatures after a drive with an IR thermometer.
Remove the caliper and check the slide pins: the upper pin is seized with corrosion.
Uneven inner/outer pad wear confirms the caliper is not floating.
root_cause: Seized caliper slide pin on the right front, causing the brake to drag and apply unevenly.
fix: Clean or replace the slide pins and boots, lubricate with high-temp brake grease, replace pads (and rotor if damaged). Replace the caliper if the piston also sticks.

common_wrong_answers.why_wrong: The car only pulls when braking, which points to the brakes, not alignment.
A master cylinder fault affects the whole circuit, not one wheel with uneven pad wear.

safety_notes: A dragging brake can overheat and fade; replace pads on both sides of the axle.

complaint: Single click when turning the key, no crank. Sometimes starts after wiggling the battery cable.
observations: Battery open circuit voltage 12.6 V
White/green corrosion on the positive terminal
Voltage at the battery posts drops to 11.8 V while cranking, but only 7 V at the starter
diagnostic_steps: Check battery state of charge and load test the battery: it passes.
Do a voltage drop test on the positive side, from the battery post to the starter B+ terminal while cranking: above 0.5 V drop means excess resistance.
Measure a drop of about 4.8 V, located at the corroded positive terminal clamp.
Clean or replace the terminal and retest: drop now under 0.3 V and the engine cranks normally.
root_cause: High resistance at a corroded positive battery terminal.
fix: Clean or replace the battery terminal clamp, protect with terminal grease, retest voltage drop.

common_wrong_answers.why_wrong: The starter is not getting enough voltage; the voltage drop test found the resistance upstream of it.
The battery passed a load test and holds 12.6 V.

safety_notes: Disconnect the negative terminal first and wear eye protection when cleaning battery corrosion.

complaint: Engine cranks but will not start. Stalled while driving earlier when hot.
observations: Scan tool shows 0 RPM while cranking
Fuel pressure normal at key-on
No spark at any coil
diagnostic_steps: Check RPM on the scan tool while cranking: 0 RPM means the PCM is not seeing the crankshaft position signal.
No spark on all cylinders plus 0 RPM points to the crank sensor circuit, not fuel.
Check the crank sensor's power, ground and signal with a multimeter or scope while cranking.
Power and ground are good, but there is no signal pattern: the sensor has failed (common when hot).
fix: Replace the crankshaft position sensor and inspect its connector and wiring for heat damage.

common_wrong_answers.why_wrong: Fuel pressure is normal; the missing RPM signal and no spark point to the crank sensor.
All coils failing at once is unlikely; the PCM is not firing them because it has no crank signal.

complaint: Battery light flickers, squealing noise on cold mornings, battery went dead twice.
observations: Charging voltage 12.4 V at idle with lights and A/C on
Serpentine belt glazed with cracks
Voltage rises to 14.2 V when the belt is sprayed with water (temporary grip)
diagnostic_steps: Measure charging voltage at the battery with the engine running: normal is about 13.5-14.7 V.
Inspect the serpentine belt and tensioner.
Note that charging voltage improves when the belt grips better, so the alternator is able to charge.
Check the tensioner spring and pulleys for wear.
root_cause: Worn, glazed serpentine belt slipping on the alternator pulley (weak tensioner).
fix: Replace the serpentine belt and tensioner, then retest charging voltage under load.

common_wrong_answers.why_wrong: The alternator charges normally when the belt grips; replacing it will not stop the slipping.

safety_notes: Keep hands clear of the belt with the engine running.

complaint: Temperature gauge climbs in traffic and at idle, but returns to normal on the highway.
observations: Coolant level full, no leaks, no white smoke
Electric radiator fan does not turn on at 105 C (221 F)
Fan runs when powered directly from the battery
diagnostic_steps: Note the pattern: overheating at low speed but fine at highway speed points to low airflow (fan), because ram air cools the radiator at speed.
Check whether the cooling fan comes on at the expected temperature, or command it on with the scan tool.
Power the fan directly: it runs, so the motor is good.
Test the fan relay and fuse: the relay is not clicking. Swap with a known-good relay and the fan works.
fix: Replace the cooling fan relay and confirm the fan cycles at the correct temperature.

common_wrong_answers.why_wrong: There is no coolant loss, no white smoke, and it runs cool at speed; the pattern points to airflow.
A failed water pump usually causes overheating at all speeds.

safety_notes: Keep hands away from the electric fan; it can start at any time, even with the key off on some vehicles.

complaint: Brake pedal feels soft and spongy after a front caliper replacement.
observations: Pedal firms up after pumping it several times
No leaks at the calipers or lines
Fluid level normal
diagnostic_steps: Confirm there are no external leaks.
A pedal that firms up with pumping points to air in the system (a compressible gas), rather than an internal master cylinder leak (which causes a slowly sinking pedal).
Bleed the brakes in the manufacturer's sequence; on ABS vehicles use the scan tool's ABS automated bleed if the modulator may have taken in air.
Recheck pedal height and feel.
root_cause: Air trapped in the brake hydraulic system after the caliper job.
fix: Bleed the brake system (including an ABS automated bleed if needed) with fresh fluid of the correct DOT type.

common_wrong_answers.why_wrong: A failing master cylinder usually gives a slowly sinking pedal under steady pressure, not a spongy pedal that firms up with pumping.

safety_notes: Do not release the vehicle with a soft pedal. Never reuse old brake fluid.

complaint: ABS and traction control lights on. ABS activates at low speed when stopping.
observations: Live data: left front wheel speed reads 0 to 8 mph lower than the other wheels and drops out intermittently
Sensor harness rubbing on the suspension near the knuckle
Sensor resistance within spec when tested still
diagnostic_steps: Compare all four wheel speeds in live data during a road test.
The left front signal drops out, which explains the false ABS activation at low speed.
Inspect the sensor, tone ring and harness.
Wiggle test the harness while watching live data: the signal cuts out where the harness is chafed.
root_cause: Chafed wheel speed sensor harness on the left front, causing an intermittent signal.
fix: Replace the sensor/harness assembly, secure the harness away from moving parts, clear codes and road test.

common_wrong_answers.why_wrong: The module is correctly reporting a bad signal from one wheel; the fault is in the sensor wiring.

safety_notes: With ABS disabled, normal brakes still work, but wheels can lock in a panic stop; advise the customer.
